 Know Thy Enemy: Revs vs Union Playoff Darkhorse Edition 
 New England and Philadelphia will seemingly be playing each other every week for the near future (again), with both teams capable of pulling off an upset in the playoffs. 
 Featured 
 Nov 21, 2026 
 by 
 Jake Catanese 
 Photo By J. Alexander Dolan 
 After the long, strange trip that was the MLS Regular season, which is to say standard operating procedures were followed and chaos occurred at normal, consistent levels, the MLS Cup Playoffs begin today at Gillette Stadium at 2 PM with the third-seeded New England Revolution hosting the sixth-seeded Philadelphia Union.
 No the play-in games that occurred midweek do not count. Which means while Gustavo Bou's walk-off play-in winner against Montreal almost 6 years ago to the day in 2020 is the last time the Revs advanced in the bracket at home; their last true playoff win was in 2014 when they won three out of four games against the Columbus Crew and RBNY to advance to their fifth and last MLS Cup Final.
 The last time the Revs were in the playoffs was against Philly as well back in 2023, with New England as the fifth seed losing the first two games, including a dull 1-0 loss at home with a late Chris Donovan winner of all things. That Revs 2020 run, however, did see them knock out the Shield-winning Union in the first round at Chester thanks to a quick first-half tandem of goals from Adam Buksa and Tajon Buchanan.
 So yes, the jokes that we play the Union every week in November will continue until morale improves or this diabolical playoff setup is abolished once and for all.
 But if we're being honest, both the Revs and Union are both very much in the mix to make a run in this postseason.
 Revolution Ready for Round 1 of Playoffs It is crunch time The Blazing Musket Sam Lattof The Revolution have been oddly consistent this year, but have rarely looked like a dominant top seed in the East. There have been a lot of injuries and moving parts this year, the usual summer slump (though it wasn't anywhere near nightmare status like most years), and it culminated in a home loss to Miami that could have seen New England finish as the second seed. Still, the Revs qualified for CONCACAF play next year, which is a tremendous turnaround and achievement for Marko Mitrovic's first year in charge.
 The Union's path to the sixth seed was far more dramatic and extreme as Philly was dead last in the East going into the World Cup break. They sacked Bradley Carnell in late May, turned things over to interim Ryan Richter, who used the midseason break to mold his team into a 15-game unbeaten juggernaut that saw the Union fly up the standings and regain the Shield-winning form they had from 2025.
 Were the roads to get to this matchup perfect? Absolutely not - it was Pennsylvania construction season combined with I-95 traffic and getting fleeced by the Darien CT rest stop McDonalds because you didn't know it's the most expensive Big Mac in the USA. While the rest of the league merely survives their ordeals traveling through the greater Northeast, the Revs and Union were born in it, shaped by it, and surviving that has made both of these teams very, very dangerous.
 That does not mean either of these teams are going to advance to just blitz Miami and Nashville out of the playoffs and into MLS Cup. These are both long-term developments in which I think both New England and Philadelphia will find themselves in that top tier in the Eastern Conference perhaps as soon as the sprint season in Spring '27 or the full '27/'28 campaign. 
 Yes, we won't be seeing young stars Cavan Sullivan or Peyton Miller long-term, sadly, with Sullivan off to join Man City and numerous clubs circling around Miller making that move inevitable. While the payoff of a successful season usually culminates in a playoff win or two, I think the Revs and Union will measure 2026 much differently than most, regardless of what happens in this matchup.
 Why Experts Predict New England to Fall to Philly in Round 1 Dax McCarty and Sacha Kljestan reveal why they think Philly will prevail The Blazing Musket Sam Lattof I have long said the Revolution's growth this year is a far better metric of success than two or three games in late November. The confidence I have in New England as an organization going forward will not change based on the results of the next few games, however many they play, and I think the same goes for Philly. The Union could have faced a season where they are blowing up a Shield-winning squad after one year and instead have righted the ship thanks to the stellar play of a lot of young players like the Sullivans, Neil Pierre, and veteran striker Milan Iloski.
 While the Union turned around their miserable first half of the year, New England survived with goal scoring by committee before a stellar second half of the year from Dor Turgeman started to really unlock the potential of the Revs' attack. Yes, there is still that element that goals can come from anywhere, and getting winger Jack Harrison back will help tremendously, but it wouldn't be unfair to say the difference between the Revs being a lock at the #2 seed or just behind Miami was 4-5 goals from Turgeman in the spring. There's just something about an in-form striker in MLS that just makes everything work better.

 Now Iloski missed a few games late for the Union, and veteran keeper Andre Blake is OUT for this afternoon's game. But by and large, it's going to be two full-strength teams for this series as New England gets a tremendous boost with Harrison and Alhassan Yusuf both returning to the lineup. This series could be decided by which of the returning players has the biggest impact overall, which would likely include Blake for Game 2. 
 I think every potential outcome in this series is possible, with either team being capable of winning the series in two games or that dastardly if needed midweek third game. I don't think you could ask for a more competitive matchup for a first-round series, and yes, someone is going to have to be eliminated. But neither team should feel disappointed at the end of this series; they've accomplished too much this year to let two games dictate ultimate success or failure.
 Here to fill us in on all things about the Union is our good friend Brady Ferguson of Philadelphia Soccer Now . We're going to try to not bother him with endless incessant chants of we play you every week which undoubtedly means we're probably going to a Game 3. Be sure to head over to their site for their half of the game coverage.
 Player Availability Report: 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs Round 1, Game 1 See who will be unavailable when the Revs battle the Union in Game 1 The Blazing Musket Sam Lattof 1) The USMNT routed Haiti 8-0 over two games during the break, but Cavan Sullivan only got one appearance off the bench...surely I wasn't the only one disappointed to not see him get more minutes. How do you think he played in his late second game shift and is a super sub role going to be the majority of his minutes in the near future? 
 Regarding the minutes, it was certainly a bit of a letdown not to see him more during the break, especially after grabbing such a large aggregate lead in the first leg. In that second match shift, he looked sharp and hungry, but with the rotation as it stands, a super-sub role seems the most likely path as he continues to adapt to the senior level. Depending on the change of manager, I hope young players like Cav, Julian Hall, and Neil Pierre continue to get chances in the starting eleven or off the bench.
 2) UConn Husky and Revs killer Andre Blake is OUT for this weekend, what are the chances he returns later in the series? How confident is the team with Andrew Rick in between the sticks based on his performances this year? 
 On the keeper situation, it's a massive loss not having Andre in there. He's such a presence. Regarding his return, he's still training with the team, and Richter said it is likely he will return for the second match of the series. Rick has been solid when needed this year, and was a large piece of the Supporter's Shield team last season. While Andre is obviously the gold standard, Rick is a great backup, and Union fans feel confident in the 20-year-old's abilities.
 3) Milan Iloski is also back and this is probably the best news the Union have had in a while. What was missing with him out of the lineup late in the year and why has he been just so darn good for the Union this year? 
 As for Iloski, his absence was definitely felt in terms of that final-third creativity. He brings comfort on the ball and decision-making that really stabilizes the attack. Additionally, pairing him with Cav up front has opened the door for Bruno Damiani, who is playing with all the confidence in the world (he just scored his first goal for Uruguay in his debut this week!). Iloski changes what the Union attack is capable of, and he understands his role in the system so well. It will be great to have him back for tomorrow's match.
 Lineup/Injuries/Predictions/Etc 
 I would think the lineup will go as follows: GK: Rick, D: (from left to right) Wagner, Harriel, Pierre, Westfield, MID: Q. Sullivan, Lukic, Jacques, C. Sullivan, F: Iloski, DamianiNo injuries to report aside from Blake. Jesus Bueno is back in the reserve rotation.Prediction: One of our writers dreamed the Union took this one in pens after a 0-0 draw, with Rick between the sticks. We are rolling with his premonition.
